scope.referenceScreening: Current AI-103 security and observability decisions, current non-AI identity/observability matches, and 17 current non-AI KQL reference decisions were screened by stem, key, concept and available code. Five selected pairs were then read with complete alternatives, explanations and code.
limitations: This is not an exhaustive all-bank semantic approval or a technical-source review.
The new AI-103 release candidates were not yet frozen. Their later hashes require fresh comparison.
No original question, source, rubric, status, review ledger or objective binding was changed.
No final originality score or independent technical/adversarial verdict is granted by this artifact.

inspectedPairs.finding: Distinct decisions at these inspected hashes.
inspectedPairs.reason: The AI-200 item diagnoses a proxy stripping traceparent after instrumentation and export already work; its alternatives concern resource naming. The AI-103 item selects nested timed spans to localize latency beyond an existing total duration. Adding a timing hierarchy does not repair lost HTTP trace context, and preserving the header does not by itself add the missing timed operations.

inspectedPairs.finding: Distinct at the current reference hash; monitor the pending AI-103 repair.
inspectedPairs.reason: The AI-200 item asks for the Python Distro initialization call with package and environment prerequisites already provided, distinguishing configure_azure_monitor from acquiring a tracer or assigning a service name. The old AI-103 item asks for three Foundry tracing prerequisites: project connection, query permissions and instrumentation. If a fresh AI-103 replacement instead tests the same Distro initialization call under reskinned prerequisites, this distinction no longer applies.

inspectedPairs.finding: Distinct decisions at these inspected hashes.
inspectedPairs.reason: The AI-200 item repairs a timestamp filter applied after summarize removed the column, while preserving one row per service. The DP-700 item reduces a shared materialize cache payload under concurrent memory pressure while preserving common branch inputs. The common phrase about moving a filter does not erase the different aggregation-grain and cache-capacity constraints.

inspectedPairs.finding: Related grouping concepts but distinct requested transformations at these hashes.
inspectedPairs.reason: The AI-200 item evaluates numeric counts for the existing role/result-code composite key. The SC-200 item must replace exact timestamps with explicit 15-minute binning while retaining DeviceId. Reading counts for an already formed composite key does not resolve the time-binning defect; the AI-200 item contains no binning decision.

inspectedPairs.finding: Distinct join-cardinality decisions at these inspected hashes.
inspectedPairs.reason: The AI-200 item already uses an explicit inner join and must avoid 2-by-3 row multiplication when computing independent per-trace counts; it requires separate preaggregation. The SC-200 item has one right-side row per key and must stop the default innerunique join from discarding distinct left rows. Its repair to inner does not solve the AI-200 multiplicity problem, while preaggregating the SC-200 input would destroy its required per-event output.
